headline: Chips Lead a Lopsided Friday as Oil Slips and Gold Climbs Into the New Week
body_html:
Markets open the week with a steadier tone than the headlines might suggest. Asian shares held their ground as worries over artificial intelligence and the Middle East receded, while the dollar firmed on expectations around the Federal Reserve. Oil is softer after President Trump signaled restraint on Iran despite fresh attacks on shipping, and gold climbed more than 1% as cheaper crude eased inflation concerns.

Friday's session, the last one completed, was lopsided beneath the surface. Of the 524 stocks we track, 285 fell and 237 rose. Semiconductors jumped 5.23% and energy added 1.01%, but homebuilders slid 2.1%, consumer shares lost 1.63% and software gave back 1.54%. Alpha and Omega Semiconductor surged 27.76% and Diodes gained 13.17%, while BlackLine tumbled 23.11%.

At the open, the question is whether chip strength carries over or gets sold into, and whether oil keeps sliding. Diplomacy is the swing factor. Mr. Trump is due to meet Qatar's prime minister, while the UAE's Anwar Gargash cautions that a US-Iran settlement looks hard to reach. Early quotes are thin, so pre-market moves deserve caution.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Traffic Stalls After Navigation Aids Destroyed
briefs.body: Iran says no unauthorised vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz overnight, after navigation aids in the waterway were destroyed. Traders will look to see whether shipping resumes normally today, since any lasting disruption would feed straight into energy pricing.

briefs.headline: Oil Eases as Washington Sounds Restrained on Iran
briefs.body: Crude drifted lower after Mr. Trump signaled he would show restraint toward Iran even as new attacks on shipping were reported. He also reportedly said an attack is unlikely if talks make progress. The softer tone is welcome for inflation-sensitive assets heading into the open.

briefs.headline: Gold Gains More Than 1% on Cooling Inflation Fears
briefs.body: Gold rose by more than 1% as the pullback in oil prices eased worries about inflation. A firmer dollar, supported by bets on the Federal Reserve, is a counterweight worth watching as the new week gets under way.

briefs.headline: Iraq Says Hormuz Export Understandings Reached With US
briefs.body: Iraq's oil minister says Baghdad has reached understandings with Washington to keep crude exports moving through Hormuz. Separately, the Khor Mor gas field has halted output after a drone attack, its operator says, and the US has asked Iraq to close most border crossings with Iran.

briefs.headline: Chip Stocks Power Friday's Lone Big Sector Gain
briefs.body: Semiconductors rose 5.23% on Friday, far ahead of every other group. Power and discrete chipmakers led, with Alpha and Omega up 27.76% and Diodes up 13.17%. Networking names such as Ubiquiti, Extreme Networks and Coherent also posted double-digit gains.

briefs.headline: Software Sold Off as BlackLine Plunged More Than 23%
briefs.body: Software shares fell 1.54% on Friday, with BlackLine down 23.11% in the worst drop in our universe. Eight more names lost more than 14%, including eXp World, Artivion and Interface. Investors will see whether the weakness spreads or stays confined to individual stories.
